en: n. a large flat area surrounded by seats where sports or entertainment events take place; a place or situation where people compete or argue; (historic) the central area of a Roman amphitheater
ex: The singer performed in a packed arena.
那位歌手在座無虛席的場館演出。

en: n. something that causes a reaction in a living thing; something that encourages someone to do something; a thing that increases activity; (plural: stimuli)
ex: Light is a stimulus for plant growth.
光是促進植物生長的刺激。

en: n. the smallest unit of a chemical substance that can exist on its own; a very small amount of something; a group of atoms that are bonded together
ex: A water molecule is made of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.
一個水分子由兩個氫原子與一個氧原子構成。

en: n. a large public meeting to support something; a recovery after a weak period; a fast exchange of hits in tennis or similar sports; v. to bring people together for a purpose; to recover your strength
ex: Thousands of people joined a rally in the city center.
數千人參加了市中心的集會。

en: vt. to think carefully about something for a long time; to look at something thoughtfully; to consider doing something; vi. to think deeply about something
ex: She contemplated the idea of changing her career.
她考慮過轉換職涯的想法。

en: vt. to accept or admit that something is true or exists; to show that you have received something; to thank someone for something; to greet someone
ex: She acknowledged that she had made a mistake.
她承認自己犯了錯。

en: n. the study of God and religious beliefs; a set of religious beliefs; the study of religion
ex: He studied theology at university to become a priest.
他在大學讀神學，準備成為神職人員。

en: vt. to hide something so that people cannot see or find it; to keep something secret; to prevent people from knowing about something
ex: He tried to conceal his disappointment with a smile.
他試圖用微笑掩飾失望。

en: a. not clear or definite; not expressed clearly; not able to think or express yourself clearly; not clearly seen or heard
ex: I only have a vague memory of that night.
我對那晚只有模糊的記憶。

en: vi. to climb or move quickly using your hands and feet; to move or act quickly in a hurry; to fight to get something that is limited; vt. to mix things together in a disordered way; n. a hurried or disorganized rush
ex: Fans scrambled to get tickets to the concert.
歌迷爭相搶購演唱會門票。

en: n. a company or business; a project, especially a difficult or important one; the ability and willingness to try new things; the activity of running businesses
ex: The government supports small enterprises with loans.
政府以貸款支持小型企業。

en: n. a work of art, music or literature that is of extremely high quality; the best work by a particular artist or writer; something done with great skill
ex: The Mona Lisa is considered a masterpiece of Renaissance art.
《蒙娜麗莎》被視為文藝復興藝術的傑作。

en: n. a mountain with a hole at the top through which hot melted rock, gas and ash can come out; a place where such activity occurs
ex: The volcano erupted and covered the town in ash.
火山爆發，火山灰覆蓋了小鎮。

en: n. a long search for something that is difficult to find; a journey to find something; an attempt to find or achieve something; vi. to search for something; vt. to look for something
ex: The knights went on a quest to find the golden cup.
騎士們出發尋找金杯。

en: n. a new business or activity that involves risk; a dangerous or exciting journey; vt. to do something risky; to say something even though it may upset people; vi. to go somewhere dangerous or unknown
ex: The company launched a new venture in Asia.
公司在亞洲展開新的事業。

en: n. money paid to someone for selling something; a group of people officially chosen to do something; an order for a work of art; the act of doing something wrong; vt. to officially ask someone to do a job; to order something to be made
ex: The agent earns a ten percent commission on each sale.
仲介每筆交易賺取百分之十的佣金。

en: a. the highest in rank, power or importance; the greatest or most extreme; n. the highest level or quality
ex: The Supreme Court made the final decision on the case.
最高法院對此案做出了最後裁決。

en: n. a secret vote in which people mark a piece of paper; a piece of paper used for voting; the total number of votes; vt. to vote on something; vi. to vote in a secret election
ex: Voters cast their ballots at the local school.
選民在當地學校投票。

en: n. a building or room where people play games for money, such as cards or roulette; a place for gambling
ex: They lost a lot of money at the casino in Macau.
他們在澳門的賭場輸了很多錢。

en: a. relating to farming; used in farming; connected with growing crops and raising animals
ex: The region is mainly agricultural, with many rice fields.
這個地區以農業為主，有許多稻田。

en: vt. to stop something for a period of time; to officially remove someone from a job or a school for a period of time; to hang something from a ceiling or a high place; vi. to stop temporarily
ex: The school suspended him for fighting.
學校因他打架而讓他停學。

en: a. very strange and unusual; strange in a surprising and often amusing way; unusual and difficult to explain
ex: He wore a bizarre costume to the party.
他穿了一件奇裝異服去派對。

en: vt. to show someone or something in a picture or story; to describe something using words or images; to represent something in a particular way
ex: The painting depicts a rural scene.
這幅畫描繪了一幅鄉村景象。

en: vt. to state something firmly; to claim your rights or authority; to behave in a confident and firm way; to say that something is true
ex: She asserted her innocence in court.
她在法庭上堅稱自己無罪。

en: a. sudden and unexpected; (of a person) rude and unfriendly in speech; (of a slope) very steep; not smooth or connected
ex: The car came to an abrupt stop.
汽車突然停了下來。

en: a. not important or serious; small and unimportant; mean and unkind about small things; minor in rank or scale
ex: They argued over petty details.
他們為瑣碎的細節爭吵。

en: n. a set of beliefs or principles taught by a religious or political group; a rule that people must follow; a principle of law; a theory that a person holds
ex: The church taught a strict doctrine to its followers.
教會對信徒傳授嚴格的教義。

en: n. a feeling that you get from touching, seeing, hearing or tasting something; a physical feeling in the body; a strong feeling of excitement or surprise; an event that causes great excitement
ex: He felt a burning sensation in his throat.
他覺得喉嚨有灼燒感。

en: n. a very old story about gods and heroes that explains natural events; a widely held belief that is not true; a person or thing that exists only in the imagination
ex: Greek myths tell stories about gods and heroes.
希臘神話講述神與英雄的故事。

en: n. a husband or wife; a person to whom someone is married; a married person
ex: You may bring your spouse to the company dinner.
你可以帶配偶參加公司晚宴。

en: n. a person whose job is to write or report for newspapers, magazines, radio or television; a person who writes about current events
ex: The journalist interviewed the president about the new policy.
記者就新政策採訪了總統。

en: vt. to put a drug or other substance into someone's body using a needle; to add something new to a situation; to put a liquid under pressure into something; to introduce a feeling or quality
ex: The nurse injected the vaccine into his arm.
護理師把疫苗打進他的手臂。

en: n. a person who comments on events in a radio or television program; a person who writes or speaks about current affairs; a person who explains what is happening in a sports event
ex: The political commentator discussed the election results on TV.
政治評論員在電視上討論選舉結果。

en: a. not obvious and difficult to notice; delicate and fine; clever in a quiet or indirect way; (of a flavor or color) very faint
ex: There is a subtle difference between the two words.
這兩個字之間有微妙的差別。

en: n. a polite expression of praise or admiration; a remark that shows you admire someone; a greeting or good wishes; vt. to say something nice about someone; to express admiration for someone
ex: He paid her a compliment on her cooking.
他稱讚她的廚藝。

en: n. the activity of managing a company or an organization; a government in power; the people who manage a business; the act of giving medicine or treatment
ex: The new administration plans to cut taxes.
新政府計畫減稅。

en: n. a person whose job is to protect someone important from attack; a person who protects someone from danger; a team of people who protect a leader
ex: The president is always accompanied by bodyguards.
總統總是有保鑣隨行。

en: n. a container with a handle and a narrow neck, used for holding liquids; (slang) a prison; vt. to put something in a jug; to cook an animal in a jug; vi. to sing like a nightingale
ex: She poured water from the jug into the glass.
她把水壺裡的水倒進玻璃杯。

en: n. a small piece that has broken off something; a small part of a whole; an incomplete piece of something; vt. to break into small pieces; vi. to break apart
ex: The vase broke into tiny fragments.
花瓶碎成了小碎片。

en: n. a solid piece of something without a regular shape; a small swelling under the skin; a large amount; a heavy, slow or stupid person; vt. to put things together in one group; vi. to form into lumps
ex: She put a lump of sugar into her tea.
她在茶裡放了一塊方糖。
